verdict.analysis: B covers more launch requirements, including delivered social assets and a sitemap scaffold, but its relative social and sitemap URLs remain unfinished. A omits the social image and sitemap entirely. Both remove the homepage indexing restriction, add descriptions, favicons, crawler rules, and recovery pages. Both supplied renders are unstyled with resource-loading errors, so neither demonstrates a visually launch-ready result. A's conversion path uses an invented, unverified mailbox; B's form targets a nonexistent backend. Both disclose these blockers. A claims browser verification without observable supporting actions; B more clearly acknowledges its verification limits, although its responsiveness and contrast PASS labels exceed the evidence. B also adds unfinished legal pages and unsupported product-workflow details. Neither fully completes the request, but B satisfies more of the specified rubric.

criteria.note: Both remove noindex/nofollow from the homepage and allow crawling.
Both provide a relevant homepage meta description preserving the core positioning.
A supplies no social image or image metadata. B delivers a PNG and image metadata, but leaves root-relative URLs; the social artwork itself is not shown in the supplied renders.
A declares a summary card with usable OG text fallback but no image. B includes large-image card metadata, title, description, and image reference, pending an absolute production image URL.
A embeds an SVG favicon in the homepage; B references a delivered SVG asset. Neither supplies observable browser confirmation of the icon.
Both supply permissive robots.txt files. B's Sitemap directive incorrectly uses a relative URL.
A omits the sitemap. B supplies XML, but every loc is relative rather than an absolute URL, leaving it unsuitable for launch.
Both deliver a custom noindex 404 document with a home recovery link. Actual unknown-route handling and HTTP 404 status remain unverified hosting dependencies.
